title: Mole Concept Conversion Triangle
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: AP Chemistry
description: Interactive triangle diagram and calculator that converts between mass, moles, and number of particles for a chosen substance, highlighting the conversion factors used (molar mass and Avogadro's number) and showing a step-by-step worked solution.

learningObjectives: Apply mole conversion factors to convert between mass, moles, and number of particles
Decide whether each conversion step requires multiplying or dividing by molar mass or Avogadro's number
prerequisites: Molar mass of elements and compounds
standards: AP Chemistry CED Unit 1, Topic 1.1: Moles and Molar Mass

controls.label: Substance
controls.description: Chooses the substance and therefore the molar mass

controls.label: Given
controls.description: Chooses which quantity is known: mass, moles, or particles

controls.label: Amount
controls.description: Value of the given quantity; particles are entered in units of 10^23

controls.label: Reset Example
controls.description: Returns to the worked example, 24.0 g of carbon

assumptions: Molar masses from standard atomic weights; results displayed to four significant figures

keyQuestions: Why must a mass-to-particles conversion pass through moles?
When do you multiply by molar mass and when do you divide?
commonMisconceptions: Multiplying by molar mass when converting grams to moles
Believing one mole of every substance has the same mass
Forgetting that Avogadro's number counts particles per mole, not per gram
assessmentOpportunities: Have students solve a conversion on paper, then verify each step with the MicroSim
